page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-3xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 32 vCPUs powered by AMD EPYC 9575F processors on the x86_64 architecture. The system features 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by three NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 144 GB of VRAM. This server operates on the KVM hypervisor and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Notably, the instance does not include local storage, requiring external storage attachments for persistent data.

The AMD EPYC 9575F CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation model. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, which enhance vector and deep learning calculations. In benchmark evaluations, the CPU demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, as well as Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics. Cryptographic and compression tasks also perform strongly, with bzip3 decompression reaching top-tier speeds.

The memory subsystem yields strong read and write bandwidth, scoring in the top 25% in PassMark memory tests. The triple NVIDIA L40S GPU configuration excels at machine learning workloads. Benchmark data shows top-tier LLM inference speeds, processing 6061.83 tokens per second for prompt processing and 129.38 tokens per second for text generation using a medium 7B model. Tradeoffs include the shared CPU allocation and the complete absence of local storage, which may impact workloads requiring dedicated host CPU cycles or high-speed local scratch disks.

Given the high density of GPU resources and system memory, this server is designed for GPU-accelerated workloads such as LLM inference, machine learning model training, image processing, and complex physics simulations. The qualitative cost efficiency of this profile is characterized by its high resource density, combining substantial GPU VRAM with a large memory footprint, making it a specialized option for parallel computing tasks that do not rely on local NVMe storage.
